answer: An agent marketplace allocates voting power by locked stake, not account count. Whether an agent trades onyx, forecasts a gale, or sells violet dye, it must lock collateral for 30 days to vote. Splitting the same stake among a thousand fake identities gives the attacker no extra voting power. To control a majority, the attacker must acquire and immobilize more stake than all honest voters combined, tying up capital and bearing its price risk.
